answer:
**Ganesha Hridayam**

According to the Mudgal Purana (Khanda 8, Chapter 49), the Ganesha Hridayam is the recitation of twenty-one names of Ganesha together with their meanings. The names listed are: Ganesha, Ekadanta, Chintamani, Vinayaka, Dhundhiraja, Mayuresha, Lambodara, Gajanana, Heramba, Vakratunda, Nijsthita, Jyeshtharaja, Ashapuraka, Varada, Vikata, Dharanidhara, Siddhibuddhipati, Brahmanaspati, Mangalyesha, Sarvapujya, and Vighnanayaka. The text states that these twenty-one names, combined with their meanings, are called the Hridayam (Mudgal Purana, Khanda 8, Chapter 49).

**Meaning of Ekadanta**

In the Ganesha Hridayam, Lord Shiva explains to Ganga:

- The syllable **"Eka"** represents **Maya** (Illusion).
- **"Danta"** (the tooth) means **Mayika** (the creator of Illusion).
- The union of both is **Ekadanta**, who resides in **Buddhi** (Mudgal Purana, Khanda 8, Chapter 49).

The Herambha Upanishad (Mantra 12) elaborates further, citing the Mudgala Purana: the word "eka" denotes maya, and "danta" denotes pure consciousness. The Lord who holds maya within him and always exists in the form of pure consciousness (Atman) is called Ekadanta by the great Vedic scholars (Herambha Upanishad, Mantra 12).

Thus, Ekadanta signifies Ganesha as the one-tusked Lord who sustains maya while remaining established in pure consciousness.

documents.page_content:
Ganga said: O Sadashiva, O ocean of compassion, please tell me the meaning of these twenty-one names so that I may know the Ganesha Hridayam.

Lord Shiva said: 

Ganesha - The letter 'Ga' represents the diverse moving and non-moving world, and'Na' represents Brahman, the supreme of the supreme. Those who reside in them are the Ganas; I bow to that one supreme Ganesha. 

Ekadanta - In the word Ekadanta, the syllable “Eka” represents Maya(Illusion) and Danta (the tooth) means Mayika (creator of Illusion). The union of both is Ekadanta, who resides in Buddhi. I
bow to Ekadanta, who is fond of devotion of his devotees. 

Chintamani - He who is the light of the consciousness, dwelling in all yet untouched by impurities, who is devoid of worldly enjoyments yet the source of all, him I bow to as Chintamani. 

Vinayaka - It means the one who is the leader of all, yet has no leader himself. I bow to him with a heart full of devotion.

Sri Eknath and Sri Ganeshayogindrawere contemporaries. Nath has described the form of Ganesha as follows:
Sri Eknathi Bhagavat (1- 2 to 15)
Salutations to Sri Ekadanta (the one-tusked). Now You alone are the absolute singularity. You show multiplicity within the one, but the underlying unity remains unbroken.
The animate and inanimate universe resides within You, which is why You are called Lambodara (large-bellied). For this reason, You truly are the kindred of everyone.
The person who beholds You, his worldly life becomes full of joy. For this reason, the revered name 'Vighnahara' (remover of obstacles) perfectly suits You.
O Lord of Ganas (Ganaraja), Your face is pure joy. The four Purusharthas are Your four arms. Shining brightly with radiant light, that is Your own divine tusk.
Both the Purva Mimamsa and Uttara Mimamsa are attached to Your ears (like ornaments). The wordless speech and others stand with folded hands at Your face.
The one who awakens seeing the entire creation as His own all at once, that is Your very seeing vision, O Vinayaka of blissful contentment.
The belly of happiness is supported, and bliss swirls in the navel. The serpent-belt of enlightenment shines, looking beautiful nearby.
The white garment of pure Sattva is beautifully tied at the waist. Ornaments of golden color truly look magnificent because of You.
You gracefully place bothPrakriti and Purusha under Your feet. Upon them, seated comfortably, You shine perfectly.
If even a momentary encounter with You occurs, no obstacle can be seen even if searched for. The one that breaks the noose of worldly existence is the very axe (Parashu) in Your fist.
The devotee who becomes dear to You through devotion, You resolve his worldly troubles. You pull him towards Yourself decisively with the goad (Ankusha).
The one who is truly completely desireless, You increase his happiness. By giving the Modak of joy, You satisfy him with Your own hands.
Smaller than the subtlest atom, Your presence is established within that. Hence the name 'Mushakavahana' (one who rides a mouse) suits You well.
Upon observing Him, He is neither a mannor an elephant. He is beyond both the manifest and the unmanifest. Knowing Him to be immutable, I respectfully bow at the beginning of this book.

16. Namo vrātapataye namo gaṇapataye namaḥ prathamapataye namaste'tu lambodarāyaikadantāya vighnanāśine śivasutāya varadamūrtaye namaḥ |

Here, by mentioning various groups, Ganesha is described as their Lord (Pati).
'Vrata' means a group of gods who are steadfast in their vows and behave accordingto disciplined rules. Their supreme lord is Vratapati.
The word 'Gana' is an indicator of Brahman. The group of the five great elements is 'Gana'. The name for the non-difference between the attributeful (Saguna) and the attributeless (Nirguna) is Gana. Their supreme lord is Ganapati.
'Prathama' means the chief or the first. All animate and inanimate creation, and gods like Surya, Vishnu, Shankara, etc., are partial aspects of Ganesha. Since theyare created from Him alone, He is the origin of all, and being their creator and controller, He is Prathamapati.
When the gods deviate from their righteous tendencies and duties, He brings obstacles in their path, bestows upon them the vision of knowledge, and then destroys those obstacles; salutations to such a destroyer of obstacles, the king of obstacles, Vratapati. Salutations to Ganapati. Salutations to Prathamapati. Salutations to Lambodara (the large-bellied one) and Ekadanta (the single-tusked one). Salutations to the destroyer of obstacles, the son of Shiva, the boon-giver (Varada) who grants everyone whatever they desire.

Phalaśruti
17. Etadatharvaśīrṣa yo'dhīte sa brahmabhūyāya kalpate | Sa sarvavighnairna bādhyate | Sa sarvatrasukhamedhate | Sa pañcamahāpāpātpramucyate | Sāyamadhīyāno divasakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayati | Prātaradhīyāno rātrikṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayati | Sāyaṃ prātaḥ prayuñjāno apāpo bhavati | Sarvatrādhīyāno'pavighno bhavati | Dharmamarthaṃ kāmaṃ mokṣaṃ ca vindati | Idamatharvaśīrṣamaśiṣyāya na deyam | Yo yadi mohāddāsyati sa pāpīyānbhavati | Sahasrāvartanādyaṃ yaṃ kāmamadhīte | Taṃ tamanena sādhayet ||

The one who recites this Atharvashirsha by contemplating and reflecting on its meaning attains self-realization. Even while possessing a physical body, he gains the power to break free from the bondage of Maya, becomes liberated in this life (Jivanmukta), and becomes one with Brahman.

He attains fearlessness from all kinds of obstacles. He attains progressively greater happiness everywhere.

He is freed from the five great sins, meaning, because of the recitation of the Atharvashirsha, he is protected fromfalling into the abyss of sins.

Brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ | Mahānti pātakānyāhuḥ saṃsargaścāpi taiḥ saha || Manusmṛti 11-54.

Killing a Brahmin (Brahmahatya), drinking liquor (Surapana), stealing (Steya), committing adultery with the guru's wife, and associating with someone who possesses these four vices—these are the five great sins.

Brahmahatya - Killing a Brahmin, causing a Brahmin to be killed, or engaging in an act that will take a Brahmin's life. A non-Brahmin falsely claiming to be a Brahmin for the sake of caste elevation. Backbiting against someone to the kingin a way that leads to their death. Telling a lie to the Guru.

Surapana - Forgetting the Vedas due to lack of practice. Condemning the Vedas by taking refuge in false scriptures. Killing a non-Brahmin friend. Consuming substances like garlic, onion, and feces, etc.

Steya - Usurping deposits, gems, gold, horses, cows, etc.

Gurupatnigamana (Adultery with Guru's wife) - Engaging in intercourse with one's own sister, a virgin, a Chandala woman, or the wives of a friend or son is a sin equal to adultery with the Guru's wife.

Fundamentally, one should not commit a sin at all. But if it happens, appropriate atonement must be performed.

Let us elaborate the meaning of gaņanātha based on puranas and khadyota bhashya of bhaskara raya makhin
गणनं गुणसंख्यानां अथ शब्दात्तु मङ्गलं
कृते तयोर्बहुव्रीहौ गणनाथ इति स्मृतः
The word gananam means count-ing, numbering, the word mangalam means auspiciousness, by the rules of euphonic combination (samāsa) called bahuvrīhi, the word means the abundanceof auspiciousness and remem-bering and respecting his great qualities is the source of good fortune and auspiciousness.

सर्वाकारा महामाया प्रकृतिर्गुणरूपिणी
तस्या सत्तादायकोयं निर्गुणो गणनाथकः
चिन्मायासंयोगरूपी सगुणो गणनाथकः

Maya is the all power of Brahman (supreme god Ganesha) and she is the one who has taken all forms. She is the universe. She is the nature (the elements, the sun the moon, mind, intellect and the feeling I) she is in the form of three gunas (sattva, rajas, and tamas) Brahman (Gananatha) is the one who gives existence to her. (i.e.) māya has no separate existence. It exists only because of the existence of the Brahman. That is why the universe (which is made of maya prakurti (nature)) is called as mithyā (that which doesn't exist - that which doesn't have a separ-ate existence.) by the Vedanta philosophers.

nirantarayam - free from obstacles / uninterrupted
nijabodhabijam - the seed of one's own knowledge/awareness

When Brahman takes a form, it is the combination of chit (absolute universal consciousness) and maya. That Brahman with form is called saguna Brahma (Brahman which has the gunas (characteristics and attributes)

nirantarayam - that which is free from interventions, obstacles, impediments.

nijabodhabijam - the seed to knowing and understanding the real self. the seed of awakening of the self.

This great wisdom is the seed of awakening the true nature of self. (i.e.) self-realisation through the under standing the ultimate wisdom, which is the only path to complete and final liberation.

I have no obstacles (which stops me), this is because I have realised the oneness with brahman and also realised there is nothing which actually exists except brahman and I am (atman is) brahman, so in this state, there are no obstacles.

I realise that everything which is perceived is brahman and every happening is also brahman and hence there is no attachment with action, because action is done by body and thought (mental action) is created by mind and I am (atman is) truly beyond body and mind so I don’t have fear of my actions going wrong because I am not activated by my fake ego or limited freewill but I have realised brahman and submerged in him, so there is no individual will but only the will of universal consciousness - supreme universal spirit (brahman) prevails. Hence, I don’t feel bound and limited but I realise I am truly liberated and free and am distinct from and beyond body and mind which is also an illusion

Because I have no individual free will left as I have realised the totaloneness with brahman my body , mind, senses etc became a tool of the supreme and hence I have no punya (merit) or sin (papa) because I am no more trapped in doer ship, whatever happens, happens by the will of brahman and whatever happens is also brahman. All the world and its happenings are like the waves of the ocean which doesn’t have any meaning without the ocean itself. Or just like reflections of sun in water, it doesn't have separate existence.

The reason for no obstacles or no sin or merit or no defective action is because of the realisation of complete oneness with brahman and hence mind also  consciously experiences the oneness also. Hence, the false ego, individual desires and fears which are the product of ignorance cease to exist. Hence the body and mind of the liberated liver, the jeevanmukta does not fall a trap of ignorance,

Though the mind and body of the gyani (self-realised soul) suffers sometimes due to past karma, the self-realised one ignores the mind and body’s sufferings because of the realisation that he the atman is brahman and is not anyways connected with sufferings of body and mind and hence he is always blissful. By realising such ultimate truth of gananatha...

क्षेमङ्करं सन्तत-सौख्यहेतुं प्रयान्ति शुद्ध गणनाथतत्त्वम् ।
विद्यामिमा प्राप्य गौरी महेशादभीष्टसिद्धिं समवाप सद्यः ।
पूज्या परा सा च जजाप मन्त्रं शम्भुं पतिं प्राप्य मुदं ह्यवाप ॥ १४॥

. Gananatha

He is bright in the color of sindhoora (vermilion), has three eyes, big belly and is covered by (wears) red cloth. He holds lasso, elephant goad, his broken tusk and shows the gesture of giving protection from all fears. He is embraced by Siddhi and Buddhi (the goddesses of success and wisdom) he has a great elephant like face, hehas one tusk (broken), he is adorned by all the ornaments, I contemplate on Ganesha who blesses his people with bliss and happiness.

gananatha is the brahman who is not bound by forms and attributes.

This is the form of lord ganesha who is the foundation of existence and the giver of ultimate wisdom.

The white garment of pure Sattva is beautifully tied at the waist. Ornaments of golden color truly look magnificent because of You.
You gracefully place bothPrakriti and Purusha under Your feet. Upon them, seated comfortably, You shine perfectly.
If even a momentary encounter with You occurs, no obstacle can be seen even if searched for. The onethat breaks the noose of worldly existence is the very axe (Parashu) in Your fist.
The devotee who becomes dear to You through devotion, You resolve his worldly troubles. You pull him towards Yourself decisively with the goad (Ankusha).
The one who is truly completely desireless, You increase his happiness. By giving the Modak of joy, You satisfy him with Your own hands.
Smaller than the subtlest atom, Your presence is established within that. Hence the name 'Mushakavahana' (one who rides a mouse) suits You well.
Upon observing Him, He is neither a man nor an elephant. He is beyond both the manifest and the unmanifest. Knowing Him to be immutable, I respectfully bow at the beginning of this book.

16. Namo vrātapataye namo gaṇapataye namaḥ prathamapataye namaste'tu lambodarāyaikadantāya vighnanāśine śivasutāya varadamūrtaye namaḥ |

Here, by mentioning various groups, Ganesha is described as their Lord (Pati).
'Vrata' means a group of gods who are steadfast in their vows and behave accordingto disciplined rules. Their supreme lordis Vratapati.
The word 'Gana' is an indicator of Brahman. The group of the five great elements is 'Gana'. The name for the non-difference between theattributeful (Saguna) and the attributeless (Nirguna) is Gana. Their supreme lord is Ganapati.
'Prathama' means the chief or the first. All animate and inanimate creation, and gods like Surya, Vishnu, Shankara, etc., are partial aspects of Ganesha. Since theyare created from Him alone, He is the origin of all, and being their creator and controller, He is Prathamapati.
When the gods deviate from their righteous tendencies and duties, He brings obstacles in their path, bestows upon them the vision of knowledge, and then destroys those obstacles; salutations to such a destroyer of obstacles, theking of obstacles, Vratapati. Salutations to Ganapati. Salutations to Prathamapati. Salutations to Lambodara (the large-bellied one) and Ekadanta (thesingle-tusked one). Salutations to the destroyer of obstacles, the son of Shiva, the boon-giver (Varada) who grants everyone whatever they desire.

Phalaśruti
17. Etadatharvaśīrṣa yo'dhīte sa brahmabhūyāya kalpate | Sa sarvavighnairna bādhyate | Sa sarvatra sukhamedhate | Sa pañcamahāpāpātpramucyate | Sāyamadhīyāno divasakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayati | Prātaradhīyāno rātrikṛtaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayati | Sāyaṃ prātaḥ prayuñjāno apāpo bhavati | Sarvatrādhīyāno'pavighno bhavati | Dharmamarthaṃ kāmaṃ mokṣaṃ ca vindati | Idamatharvaśīrṣamaśiṣyāya na deyam | Yo yadi mohāddāsyati sa pāpīyānbhavati | Sahasrāvartanādyaṃyaṃ kāmamadhīte | Taṃ tamanena sādhayet ||

The one who recites this Atharvashirsha by contemplating and reflecting on its meaning attains self-realization. Even while possessing a physical body, he gains the power to break free from the bondage of Maya, becomes liberated in this life (Jivanmukta),and becomes one with Brahman.

He attains fearlessness from all kinds of obstacles. He attains progressively greater happiness everywhere.

He is freed from the five great sins, meaning, because of the recitation of the Atharvashirsha, he is protected from falling into the abyss of sins.

Brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ | Mahānti pātakānyāhuḥ saṃsargaścāpi taiḥ saha || Manusmṛti 11-54.

Killing a Brahmin (Brahmahatya), drinkingliquor (Surapana), stealing (Steya), committing adultery with the guru's wife, and associating with someone who possesses these four vices—these are the five great sins.

Brahmahatya - Killing a Brahmin, causing a Brahmin to be killed, or engaging in an act that will take a Brahmin's life. A non-Brahmin falsely claiming to be a Brahmin for the sake of caste elevation. Backbiting against someone to the king in a way that leads to their death. Telling a lie to the Guru.

Surapana - Forgetting the Vedas due to lack of practice. Condemning the Vedas by taking refuge in false scriptures. Killing anon-Brahmin friend. Consuming substances like garlic, onion, and feces, etc.

Steya - Usurping deposits, gems, gold, horses, cows, etc.

Gurupatnigamana (Adultery with Guru's wife) - Engaging in intercourse with one's own sister, a virgin, a Chandala woman, or the wives of a friend or son is a sin equal to adultery with the Guru's wife.

Fundamentally, one should not commit a sin at all. But if it happens, appropriate atonement must be performed.
